utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam Registrar. Could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good morning to you. Mr. Oric, can you follow the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, ladies and gentlemen. Yes, I can follow the proceedings in my own language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down. And good morning to you, too. Appearances for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Jan Wubben, lead counsel for the Prosecution. I'm here together with Gramsci di Fazio, attorney, and Dr. Fagel, the expert for the Prosecution consulting us; also our case manager, Mrs. Donnica Henry-Frijlink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Wubben, and good morning to you and your team. And to you, Mr. Fagel. Appearances for Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to the learned friends from the OTP. My name is Vasvija Vidovic. Together with Mr. John Jones, I appear for Mr. Naser Oric. We have with us this morning our legal assistant, Ms. Jasmina Cosic, our CaseMap manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts, and our Defence expert, Mr. Bilic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Vidovic. And good morning to you and your team. And to you, Mr. Bilic. So any preliminaries? Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Very short, Your Honours. This morning, the expert of the Prosecution, Mr. Fagel, by accident met Dr. Kerzan in the lobby. They shook hands and as meeting each other and greeted each other and exchanged some words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exchanged some words? What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I wasn't present at that meeting. I understood that it was short, and Dr. Kerzan expressed that he was surprised that the Prosecution had now -- had no questions, and the response by our expert was apparently, "You did well." Then Dr. Kerzan expressed, "Well, we should meet soon. That would be nice." Something like that. I'm not a witness, Your Honour. And then our expert told," Well, better not," and that was the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Wubben. Ms. Vidovic, are you interested in hearing more about this?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. That's quite enough. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. So thank you for the information, for the loyalty, Mr. Wubben, and Mr. Fagel. Let's bring the witness in. Any preliminaries on your side? Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, is it possible that before the cleanup session, that there is a short break because Ms. Patricia Sellers would like to join us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. And we need a short break ourselves any way. Thank you. But let's try and finish as early as we can today because I have an emergency at home, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Dr. Kerzan. We are proceeding with your testimony this morning and hopefully finish. May I just remind you you are testifying in terms of or pursuant to the solemn declaration that you made yesterday, which you don't need to repeat today. Mr. Jones will be proceeding with his questions. Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And good morning, Dr. Kerzan. I hope your cold is better this morning.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's quite better, thank you very much. And good morning to you too.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm going to start taking us right back to a passage in Ellen. I'm not sure if you have that with you. It's page 61. And the heading is "clarity of expression." And it's the first paragraph. And I'll just read that: "When expressing any qualified conclusion it will be apparent that more than one possibility is allowed for, although one is more likely than the other or others. It will make the report more clear to those for whom it is written if these are spelt out and the greater probability of one rather than the others is stated. For instance, if the conclusion that there is a high probability that the writings are by one person, the converse is that coincidental match cannot be ruled out but is nevertheless very unlikely. This should be referred to in the interests of clarity in the report." Firstly, do you agree with what's written there?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, in your report, you don't express the converse possibilities, do you? For example, the P13, when you found that that was probably the author of the reference in questioned signatures being the same person, you didn't say that possibly they were not the same person.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did not write that the opposite possibility because I believe it goes -- that goes without saying. If you go with probability, it is not -- there is always another possibility. That's why I did not. It's an omission which is I don't think very important, but if you think so it's probably -- I probably should have done that, as you say.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's to make this point really: That you did not leave unspoken the possibilities that did exist that the reference and questioned signatures were not by the same person. Even though those possibilities exist, you didn't state them in your report?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can we refer to the document number, just a second. P14 and P37 which I decided inconclusive. I explained yesterday why I decided that I cannot do -- be -- really be certain. But within that positioning, inclusive, I believe it is also -- it is also understood that possibility exists. I believe so. I might be wrong, but I believe this exists, particularly in the case of P14.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The possibility, in other words, that the author is not the same?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I cannot say anything about that. I do think it's inconclusive. But a possibility, certainly it is a possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thanks. We are going to come to that. For now I'll ask you to point to some features of the reference samples, and so it would help actually if you would put some pages of your report on the ELMO and then use the pointer as well, which you should have. And I'm going to suggest to you that there are some consistent and distinct features in the reference samples and see if you agree. Let's start with image 4, which is page 19 of your report. And for the record, this is 02066403.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm going to suggest seven or so features which I suggest are in this sample. Now, the first is that the R is not connected to the O. And perhaps you can point to that with a pointer and confirm that for us.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean R and O, that they are not connected?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: There is a space between there.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, here.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Second, I suggest that the horizontal tapers at the end?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you -- I did not understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The horizontal.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I don't have what you say on the --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Okay. The horizontal line tapers towards the end.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean it is getting lighter?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And now in the "ch" there is a dip or a kink or I'm not sure how you would describe that, but I think you even pointed that out yesterday. And perhaps you could point to that now, the bottom part of the "ch"?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, the way it goes in, there is a kink; do you agree?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kink?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Or a - what's a better way to put it? - a dip. You see, it's not fully rounded. It goes in. If you could put your pen there, we'll all see. On the "ch," the bottom part of the "ch," roughly where arrow 7 is.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean that there is some --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's out of focus now. It goes in, the "ch." As it comes around, it then dips inward towards the horizontal. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really know what you're pointing at.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Can you put your pen on the --

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. Now move it a little to the left --

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean here?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No, left. There. You see where it goes in.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is within this loop, you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The loop goes like that.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not a loop. It's the ending of the e-u-e [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Okay. That point, anyway, where you're pointing to.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's a distinctive feature; correct?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is quite a distinctive feature, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. And -- well, how would you refer to that so that we can refer to it easily later, that feature?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not easy to say that in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'll call that a kink in the "ch," so we'll know what I mean. Now also is there not - and I think you referred to this yesterday - a deep penetrating closing stroke on the O which is almost like a third vertical? I think you mentioned that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's here.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yeah. In fact, we can see it better on image 5 and 6 on the next page even. Yes, you see it comes --

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Comes right in and it's almost like a third vertical?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the same goes for the next --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. There is no full stop, we can agree on that, in any of the reference samples. Would you agree that the, what we were calling garland, the wavy bits --

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: -- are not in the nature of zigzag. They are more in the nature of garlands. Would you agree with that, it's a garlanded style?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular -- they differ a little bit from one to the other. But I don't know what you mean by "garland." You mean what was translated as a wave-like --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, Wave-like rather than zigzag.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we went through this yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You don't need to agree on that if you don't agree --

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really know what you're trying to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We'll leave that feature. We've identified four or five already. Do you agree that the O in all the reference samples more ellipsoid and large rather than circular?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Rather than ellipsoid, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. And certainly it's never written "Naser Oric," is it? It's only ever a surname? You don't have, as we had in one of the questioned samples, two names?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I referred to theses signatures yesterday, you can clearly see that N is within the O which is a beautiful handwriting feature.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So are agreed, then, and we can go through the other images of the sample signatures, but there are four or five characteristics there which are in all of them. The R is not connected to the O, and you can see that on images -- clearly on images 5 --

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. You go to images 5 and 6, page 20.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it's almost connected on image 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's page 20, images 5 and 6. If you could put that on the ELMO, that would be helpful. That again the R and the O is not connected. The tapering horizontal. There is the dip in the "ch," and there is a deep penetrating closing stroke on the O, and the O is ellipsoid. All the same features we saw in the last reference sample; correct?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I have the wording on the screen too?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Basically means we need to zoom out a little bit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, no. I don't have what is written --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, the transcript?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The transcript, yes. I would like to have both, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not possible in your case.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I can take it just one at a time then.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday I had it. That's why I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What does he have in the big monitor, in the -- was it off yesterday as well or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I can have something -- it's easier if I can re-read the question and ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it okay now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. And now just to check that this image is not the one we just saw. Is this image 4 that we have?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one is image 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Image 5. That's also fine.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is image -- let me see which one is that. Okay, no. Yeah, sorry. Reference signature 405, so image is number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Six, okay. So taking six, which is a different one from the one we looked at, again, aren't all the features there that we can do them quickly but one by one, R is not connected to the O?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a second, please. You said six features.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, we'll take them one by one. I think there -- you didn't agree with garlands, so we can say seven features. And I'll count them for you. Firstly, R not connected to the O; correct?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Secondly, tapering horizontal?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: What I was calling the kink in the "ch." Do you agree that's there?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a second. I would like to add here again. It is not a kink in the "ch." It is the ending of the E.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Okay. So we will call it the ending of the -- a kink in the ending of the E?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not a kink. It's the ending of the letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not something particularly -- which has nothing to do with the letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. It's not present in any of the reference -- in the questioned signatures, that's my point, and we'll come to that.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And that's why I need to refer to it somehow. The ending of the E. I suppose that's the ending of the I?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I, yes. Sorry, it's my English.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's fine. That feature, deep penetrating closing stroke on the O, can you agree?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No full stop?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No full stop. Could you please explain that? I didn't --.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: In the reference samples yesterday, we saw that there was a punctuation mark at the end of some of the signatures as they had been written with a full stop?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the dot at the end of it?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And the O is ellipsoid and rather large; correct? That's a feature which is present?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, I suggest to you that those features are present in all of the reference signatures, and rather than going through them all, if you disagree, then let me know. Certainly we can look image 7 and 8. I suggest that the same features are there: R is not connected to the O, tapering horizontal --

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we go -- if we start with image 1, you will see that the thing you call kink in "ch" is not present on this reference material. If you agree. If you don't, then --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Point to it.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. You may see that this kink, as you called it, or whatever it is outside of this loop on the "ch." Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. We'll agree on that for image one. Do you agree -- If you keep the image there for a moment, image one.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You agree, don't you, that the other features are there. In fact, if you look very closely, the R is not connected to the O. It's very near but it's not actually connected?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not connected. It starts over here lightly and then goes down.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. And there is a tapering horizontal?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I just have a note here? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Okay. I'm not going to go through all the reference signatures unless we really need to. I want to move on to the questioned samples, but of course we'll bear in mind those features which we've just looked at. Now, I'm going to -- I'm more interested in those documents where you gave an opinion, but I do need to start, nonetheless, with P3?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: P3 is -- it's the image on page 22, image 9. Now, here you said that -- well, you reached the conclusion of inconclusive, if one can put it that way. And your explanation of inconclusive is in your report at page 6: "Similarities, identical handwriting features and differences between the questioned and referenced material occur with the same frequency, which makes it impossible to either confirm or disprove whether or not the questioned and reference signatures can be assumed to have been written by the same person." And, in fact, you also explain on page 5 of your report. In English it's about ten lines down: "In cases where the handwriting signature is found to contain the same level of identical and differentiating features, it is impossible to prove whether the questioned and reference handwriting signature materials are identical or not." I suggest there you're talking again about your inconclusive result, where you have the same numbers of similar and different features. Do you agree that's what "inconclusive" means in your report?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's one of the definitions on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. So, in fact, in P3 when you say "inconclusive," in fact what you found is as many similarities as differences to the reference samples, did you not?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did explained yesterday that the inconclusive in this case, I decided to go to inconclusive because of the fact that this particular questioned signature is a photocopy of the very bad quality, and I could not see the characteristics of this -- of the signature. That was the reason for inconclusive.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to come to that in a second. But doesn't that mean, first of all, that your report is incomplete because your definition of inconclusive doesn't provide that as a possible reason for using that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say incomplete, but I could have clarified this matter. The matter of impossibility of actual examination. I did not explain that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Surely, you've done tens of analyses of handwriting and signature samples, and presumably you're using the same scale each time, using the same working template. So is this -- this incomplete explanation, is this in all the reports which you do on handwriting, or is this something which has just occurred in this case?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is the scale of conclusions I always use. I do not change it a lot. I mean, there can be some small differences but not -- no. But you have to realise that in this particular case I take a look at those, and usually I decline to do photocopies anyway. Photocopies are not material, in my opinion, for an expert to be used for handwriting or signature examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's look at your explanation for why you've come to the inconclusive result. You say: "Since the copy is of poor quality and the signature is to a large extent covered, it is my conclusion that no assumption" -- and I'm afraid we do have the word, at least in English, "assumption" there, "no assumption can be made concerning the identity of the signature." Now, I put it to you that that is not the explanation for --

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I see my originals, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please break between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. We'll do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I was quoting from the --

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: -- penultimate sentence.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was going to your "assumption" word. In the original there is no "assumption." It's a little bit of the problem with translation. I didn't notice before. If I can give you a direct translation from Slovenian, if you agree. I have this in the ultimate version. It's a little bit different.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Certainly, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The signature has also been copied," it says here, and I quote now, I'm trying to do a translation. "Part of the questioned signature is covered by the stamp impression, so only relatively small part is -- can be seen. As the photocopy is a bad quality, and because the signature is -- is covered, I think -- I think that the examination is not possible and that authorship of this signature cannot be either -- neither proved either" -- just a second. "Cannot be" -- "the authorship of this signature cannot be established. Thank you very much." That's what I said. There is no "assumption" in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Okay. That's fine. My comment is this: Firstly, yes, this is a photocopy, but you've analysed copies before, haven't you? For example, in Brdjanin, you've analysed copies and given conclusions?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but this was not an expert opinion. There was just a guide-lines for the -- for the -- for the -- this -- yes, for the -- not --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Don't worry about the Brdjanin report. That's less important than this, really. Yes, the poor quality consists of flecks of toner which we can see. But I suggest that that doesn't impede analysis. You can see the O; you can see it's more circular than the ellipsoid Os in the reference sample. You can see that there is no closing stroke on the O. You can see there's no -- what I was referring to as the kink in the I; you can see that's not there. In fact, there are features which you could have analysed and reached conclusions about. Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are some features which one can see but I may -- I may very much disagree with your findings on this one. Because, I mean, defining ellipsoid, or round, is a difficult thing to do, and I don't see here a big difference. And if we go into an analysing, but I don't want to go, you could see that I think the penetration here in -- within the O is quite deep. It just doesn't cover the left but the right line, so it's -- but, again, it's a photocopy. This is what I -- this is an assumption. I can just -- well, it's guessing. That's why I did not want -- did not want to go further with this examination at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. My point, though, is that you certainly could analyse those features and you could measure angles as well, could you not?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I disagree with you. I cannot do a proper examination of this -- this signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Okay. We can move on to P4. And that's image 10. Let's have a look at P4, image 10, which is on the same page. Now, here, your opinion is that the questioned and reference signatures are written by the same person?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And therefore, or because, rather, the conclusions strongly support that assumption. Now I want to ask you first a question, we discussed this yesterday, that your practice of adding your opinion to this finding of -- the "strongly supports" finding is not recommended by ENFHEX. So which part, in fact, should we pay attention to when we look at your analysis? Should we look at "strongly supports" or should we look at your opinion, or do they mean the same thing to you?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I explained yesterday, the opinion consists of two things: One are the findings; and then at the end of it, I give my opinion, which is a subjective opinion, what we clarify yesterday. And this is the part from -- going from, "Therefore, it is my opinion." I would say that the main -- or the conclusion to strongly support the assumption or the proposition would be right or ... so it's -- it is just the -- in my point, not in yours. You yesterday put it that it is illogical. But from my point of view it's that if I find filings that strongly support, I can give the opinion that this is so. This is just my adding of -- to clarify questions of the -- of the -- of the -- that were put to me. The reason for that, if I may finish that -- excuse me. The reason for that is that the expert -- I could have made this definition so odd nobody could understand it. I put that at the end of it just to clarify things. So I don't think it's necessary to go into that each time. I mean, I hope it's understandable now. I -- it's the second time I'm trying to explain that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I will do it again, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Certainly, no. There's -- I'll leave a pause. There is no need to labour the point. It's simply this, really: This Trial Chamber and us, we have to try to assess your findings.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And we have this phrase "strongly supports" which, of course, one could contrast with weakly supports or doesn't support at all, something which means something in layman's terms. And so it's really just to have this confirmation from you that we can take those words strongly supports the proposition and take that from your report and focus on that. That means the same thing or it's detachable from your final opinion. Would that be fair to say?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, when we come to this signature, you say the sole difference is this full stop at the end, and you explained that by virtue of the nine-year gap. Now before I proceed to that explanation, adding a full stop is not insignificant, is it? It's an extra gesture and an extra stroke. It's something which we can visualise quite clearly, someone signing --

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: -- and then [indiscernible] the spot. It's significant, is it not, and rare?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot -- I cannot say it's rare. It can be significant; I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, have you --

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: But if I may -- if I may explain this dot a little more, if I can? You just can't take one sample and another sample. You have to take a look at all the samples. If one has a dot and the other has not a dot, it means that this feature is not consistent through all of that. Do you agree with that? So ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We see this in several questioned signatures.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, have you ever come across in the literature or in your own practice someone punctuating their signature and then ceasing to do so due to a lapse of time? Have you ever actually come across that or is that just a hypothesis?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the lapse of time has not a lot to do with that. But, yes, the signatures do change and the features do change and the features can be -- somebody can cease to use certain feature or somebody can add new features to his signature. It's quite common, not necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sure. Now, if you had reference samples from 1992 with no full stop, you'd revise your explanation, wouldn't you? You would be more sceptical about whether this was the same author?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is -- this is -- this is a hypothetical questions. I don't know, because I didn't see those from 1992. If you can provide it to me, I can give you an answer. Otherwise, it's difficult to answer. It's clearly hypothetical questions -- question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, it is hypothetical. But sometimes experts can answer hypotheticals.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know. It is possible, but it is not -- I can't say nothing more than that it's possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, this nine-year gap between the reference samples and the questioned samples is in fact a hindrance to analysis, isn't it? It's not a tool which helps your analysis. Would you accept that?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hindrance meaning limitation? Okay. Yes, it can be. There is no rule what limitation is or what limitation is not. So I cannot say conclusively it is a limitation, but it can be a limitation always.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And here you've turned that limitation, have you not, into an explanatory tool; namely, that the full stop disappears due to the passage of nine years. So what was a hindrance or an obstacle now helps your analysis; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Should say helps not hems; is it right?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say I used an explanatory tool. It -- I pointed to that possibility because the -- this is the -- the -- the feature I didn't find on the -- on the reference samples. But as I said before, I believe it's a small feature, and if one small feature is not there, I -- this particular feature, I presumed it is the matter of this time lapse. Of course, I cannot be sure about that because I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And you presume that despite the fact that P158, which is also from 1992, has no full stop at the end?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Actually, the fact that P158 does not have that full stop or dot at the end shows me that this feature probably is not so prominent as you're trying to point.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, my suggestion to you on this is that what you should have done to be objective is actually simply record this as a difference rather than trying to find some way to explain it. Perhaps you wouldn't consider it significant but simply record that it is a difference and not search for some explanation. Do you agree that would be more objective?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I did that. Are you trying to imply that I didn't point that as a difference? I mean, I did point that as a difference. Your I'm implying that I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You sought an explanation for it?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I tried to find an explanation, yes. But anyway, I did note it, I showed it with a different colour on my image, so it's ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. It's arrow 11 on images 10, 14, 15, 16.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the other --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And my point really is this: Is weren't you focussing on similarities between the reference samples and the questioned samples? Looking for similarities and discounting differences whenever you found them?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would hardly agree with you, otherwise I wouldn't -- wouldn't decide for inconclusive with a couple of other signatures, like P14, which is clearly inconclusive, or P37. I completely disagree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Let's deal with P4. I suggest to you that actually there are many more differences than similarities, and we've looked in the reference samples of -- at six or seven of those. Do you agree here that the R is connected to the O and it's connected in quite a definite way with quite a --

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not connected. It is not connected. It touches, but it's not connected. It's the other stroke. What you're looking for here is not the -- the pure image of it but you're looking the stroke. You have one stroke which is O. If it would go from O directly as a stroke into the R, then you would have connections, but you don't. The O stops and then it is started again. It can start with the -- with the -- the -- it almost touches here, O, but it doesn't really. It's a bit -- a bit up --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: My point --

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very near.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: My point is this: In none of the reference samples do we see a stroke going between -- there we go. You can see there is a gap. There is always a gap between the O and the R?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but this gap is not -- this gap is hardly bigger than the gap on the P4. And the same goes here -- just a second. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry, we can't actually see -- there we go. Again, a big gap between the O and the R --

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a big gap, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I put to you, it's always there.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not always there. I just -- I'm showing you that it is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we may disagree about that.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: In terms of the horizontal line on this one, P4, it's not tapering but blunt, isn't it? It's completely regular, and it doesn't taper or get any narrower at the end. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with that. But I do believe this is the -- that is the problem of the writing utensil, as I pointed out yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, do you know also what that can indicate, a blunt line? It may mean slow movement and even imitated movement of someone who it actually going along very slowly rather than doing a quick line?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it can, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'd like to refer to page 35 of David Ellen on slowly made --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Incidentally while you're making use of this David Ellen excerpts or extracts, we forgot to give it a --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- An exhibit number yesterday. So this will become Defence Exhibit D1023. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's this part, the last three lines, under "slowly made simulations." "In trying to produce a careful and slowly made free-hand copy such variations in pressure" - and those are the ones referred to earlier in the passage - "are difficult to reproduce. Because they arise from the speed of natural movement, they cannot be produced when the hand is moving slowly and is consciously controlled to imitate an unfamiliar pattern. Instead, the slowly moving pen is maintained at a more constant pressure on the paper, and the written line is therefore more even in width and its end not tapered but blunt." Do you agree with what's written there?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. But you're taking one part of the David Ellen's quote as a sole proposition. You have to read it all over again. You should take it as a whole, and you should also take the signature itself as a whole. The signature --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I simply wanted your agreement if you agree to this, and I think you have just agreed to it that's --

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I agree. But --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: -- Tapering line can be indicative of a slowly made --

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I would like to pay attention to the word "can." It does not -- it doesn't say it does. It says "can." It's a bit of a difference, I think, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Of course. And did you notice that?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That this line was not tapering but blunt? Now, let's look at the I, what I was calling the kink in the I.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It certainly doesn't appear in the loop, does it? That's an ellipsoid, regular ellipsoid loop on the "ch"?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it doesn't. It is just a moment before it, the ending of the E is -- or I, sorry, I, is just before. It is -- may I point it out, if I can finish it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is exactly the same, the same, the same movement of the hand as it is present on the -- on the -- on the reference material. It's the same movement. It can move left, right, and if I remember correctly, there is also a reference signature that does not have that, if I can point that out. So it is not necessary, it is not ruled that is so strong to not to have possibility to have doubt.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That is different from what is usually found in the reference samples?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it does -- it does appear in the reference sample and that is important.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Okay. Again, the O here. It's not ellipsoid and large. It's actually much more round than in the reference samples; do you agree?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is your definition. I mean, I -- define ellipsoid.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, in fact --

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is quite ellipsoid, if you ask me.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: In fact, you do mathematical measurements. You could, with the diameter you could in fact see, couldn't you, that that is more round than the ellipsoid Os in the reference samples?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see a significant difference. I didn't see that when I did my examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, let's look at the closing stroke on the O, which you called yesterday a penetrating loop, and today you agreed it's sometimes almost like the third vertical. Here it appears nothing like that?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this particular signature, there is nothing like that, yes, I fully agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. But I put it to you that there are as many differences in this signature as there are similarities and that you've picked the similarities and you've ignored the differences?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I disagree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: For the rest of this document, have you -- did you look at it for signs of tampering in accordance with the third part of your mandate?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must admit that I was very much preoccupied with the handwriting, and I don't know which document that is. I do believe that I didn't find any significant tampering with the document. But this is a document which has I think this -- this covering --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No. This has different changes. May I put it to you firstly, just as a general matter, let's imagine there is a document which says that prisoners or persons should be arrested and someone crosses out "arrested" and puts "killed." That's tampering and it's pretty significant tampering, because it changes the whole meaning?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, are you trying to imply that this happens in this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm getting there. Do you agree with what I just put to you? That that's tampering, if you change a word and change the meaning of a document?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If you change the meaning of the document, it would be -- well, it would -- define tampering, first of all. Well, if I write the document and I change it, did I tamper myself with the document? It is tampering in this way. But if there is an error which is corrected, is that tampering? I don't know. It's legal -- it's a legal thing here. So it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Let me take this one point at a time. Exactly. You have to know what was written behind, and you don't know, do you, and leave aside this document, the ones where there had been Tipex and changing. You don't know what was written beforehand, so you can't say whether or not there was tampering?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I just take a look at my copies, please? Because I don't know which document you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We can stick with this document, P4.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I want to take my copy out just to take look at which one is different.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is your suggestion that it was tampered with here?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, here look at 10. There is obviously something, [B/C/S spoken], [B/C/S spoken] in ten has been typed over something which was there before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Which image -- pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, we were on P4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: P4, yeah, that's what we have. But the image number.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't have an image of that feature.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We have to look at the document itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see. All right. Okay. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you have the full document --

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just have photocopy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Just for example there, you can see [B/C/S spoken] has been added, and you can see under Roman numeral II where it says [B/C/S spoken]. That appears to have been typed over?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not a good photocopy. I don't see that, but I will take it that you probably are right. It's --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will come back to this point with the Skelani document. I think that's -- probably better illustrates it. There is no need for the witness to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Up to you. But if the witness wishes to see this P4 in it's original form, we can make it available.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm just trying to see which document that is. I cannot perform examination here anyway, so it doesn't make sense to -- to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No one is expecting you to do that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would like to hear -- to add something within this -- within this -- there is -- I was given relatively short time for this analysis. I usually take -- take me more than a month to do such analysis, so I may have concentrated far more on the -- on those signatures than on the other parts of the document. But still I don't think I -- I -- I did omit a lot in this document. I don't really think so. I didn't find any -- anything that was written before. I didn't find this, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's my point really. And it's not a criticism that you had to work in a hurry. But in -- for this document and others, for this one you say: "There is no visible evidence the document has been falsified, i.e., manipulated," and I'm really wondering what for you would be such a sign, if you have documents where words had been scrubbed out and other words written on top. How can you say that that isn't a sign of manipulation or falsification?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen any torn parts of the paper except for down -- what is on the -- on the -- on the lower portion which is actually -- had been burned. Otherwise usually with a typewriter, you can see -- if you want to erase typewriter, you would need some mechanical tool. And with a mechanical tool and such a thin paper, as it was used on this particular document, I believe I should have seen the torn paper fibres which I didn't find. But, again, I -- I may have omitted that, but I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We'll come back to that in a moment where there is more clear. Now the signature on this document is with a fountain-pen. Do you know what ink was used or what instrument to do the protocol number in the top left-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I write that down. Handwritten document number using a ball-point pen, I wrote. But I don't remember the document itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm looking under P4 and I'm not seeing that.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: P4, line 3: "The questioned document is a type print which signature and handwritten document number using a ball-point pen." This ball-point pen is referring to handwritten number. It is more clear in the Slovenian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Thank you. I'd like to move on to P13. We are finished with that document. And that's image 11, page 23 on your report.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just show P13. Do you agree, it's the right one?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. And one minute, please. Now here you've said it's probably written by the same person, the questioned signature, the same person as the author of the reference samples?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a second, please. Just trying to close so I can see the image.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now again this is from 1992. There is no full stop, but I take it you're saying that to you that was insignificant?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the fact that it's not full stop, that is consistent with reference signature. Wouldn't that be so? I mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Are you allowed to draw both conclusions, that that consistency supports your conclusions, whereas for P4, P75, the inconsistency doesn't affect your conclusions at all? Are you being consistent there?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question, to be honest.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Fine, I'll rephrase it. You say, Well, this is -- there is no full stop here, so that -- that's an indication that it's the same author because the reference samples don't have a full stop. But that didn't -- the presence of a full stop didn't prevent you with P74, P75, P73 from concluding it's the same person. So are actually using that as an analytical tool or aren't you?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I just -- I'm just -- I'm just not finding this feature. It's -- I don't know what you define as an analytical tool here.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your theory is that the full stop disappeared after nine years. That's when the person -- the person had stopped using the full stop by then. This is from 1992. Surely they should have been using a full stop if they are being consistent with P4, P75 and the others.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that. It is a feature that is not consistent in -- also in 1992. That is what I was trying to say. And I actually explained that before, when we discussed this full stop or dot.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Okay. For the horizontal, it actually has a strange downward sloping line at the end, doesn't it? We've never seen that before, have we?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah -- no, you're -- yes, I agree with that. But you have to realise that -- that now you are implying that every single signature would have to have all the same proportions exercised in the same way. That's what you're implying. It can happen with a signature that the line goes a little low, a little high and so on. That's the natural variability of a signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I understand that. What I'm putting to you is that wherever there are differences you simply say, Well, this is due to the natural variation --

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not a difference. You said it's a difference. It is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, here, would you agree that this is possibly not the signature of Naser Oric? Or the signature the -- the author of the reference and questioned signatures --

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You might have noticed I have left place for this interpretation within my -- within my report. I didn't phrase it that way, as you put it, but, yes, I agree with you on that one. But I don't think it's very likely.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Okay. Well, on page 11 of your report as you were discussing this document, you refer to "ink-stains that probably result from the use of a poor writing implement."

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, in fact, isn't that a well-known phenomenon of -- known as blobbing or a gloop [sic]? And I can refer to Ellen just to show I'm not inventing these terms. It's on page 12 of Ellen. Ink lines -- and it's the last two sentences. "When a ball-point pen changes direction to form a curve, it may deposit excess ink immediately after making the curve. The positions of these goops in the writing line can indicate the direction of the pen." And then figure two shows these goops. And we can see: "Note: A striation crossing from the inside of the curve to the outside and the goop after the pen has completed the curve." That's, in fact, what we are looking at, isn't it? It's not a bad -- it's not a poor writing implement. It's a well-known phenomenon of blobbing or glooping [sic]?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, you have to -- you have to read all the -- the -- the -- this part of his -- of his -- of his -- in his book. Of course, it can -- it can be that, but it also can be the matter of the -- of the writing utensil. And I believe, because I -- I was thinking about that when I was analysing that, but one of those is pretty good, is shown on the very beginning of the -- of the line, as you may see here, and that this -- as you say, as it's said here goop, indicates that is a problem of the writing -- of the writing utensil. When the person put the pen on the paper, the excessive ink goes out. So whenever -- and the other goop, which is on the top of the -- of this -- of this -- of O, is on the point -- is in the point -- on the point where the -- because of the nature of the loop, the writing utensil slows down, and then when it slows down again, the excessive deposit of ink can happen. But, again, I say can, or may have. It's not something which is necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. So you're familiar with the features of writing with a ball-point pen, and I think you told us yesterday that a signature is executed differently with a fountain-pen than with a ball-point pen, in terms of pressure?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You can see because of the pressure, the pressure can be lighter with a fountain-pen. It is the -- the lines are different. The lines are more smooth. They do not -- they do not change when -- when the pressure is lesser -- is lesser. They don't change so much. I think I explained that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. You agree that there is a difference in the pressure used, just to summarise, or do you not agree?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The pressure is a bit different, but the pressure is not an absolute thing here. The pressure exercised within the signature changes all the time. One line is stronger, the other is less strong. Using a fountain-pen you don't have to -- to -- to put more pressure -- so much pressure as you use when you use -- when you use a ball-point pen, because the ball-point pen is a different utensil. But, of course, the dynamics of this should exist in -- I mean, exists in all of them, but it also -- with a fountain-pen or some other writing utensils, but with a fountain-pen it's not as easy detectable, as a fountain-pen has liquid ink. That's what I was talking about yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. Which is just to anticipate, isn't it, you didn't have any reference samples of signatures made with a fountain-pen?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, unfortunately I didn't have.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Shouldn't that have made you more cautious in your conclusions about signatures made with a fountain-pen?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I was very cautious anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Let's look at this document, still with P13, about the question of manipulation. Did you not notice that there it was an imprint of the word "Oric" on the document, a concave impression on the document and perhaps -- sorry, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And perhaps actually the witness should be provided with the original, if that's possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you could put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. If you looked at the left-hand corner -- sorry, the left-hand side, it's sideways to the text?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you point that to me? I don't --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry, if we move it back a bit. Now if we stop there. Do you see where --

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just tell me where.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Do you see [B/C/S spoken], the bottom line?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, go down from there and see, a -- what's written perpendicularly, you'll see an O. Yes, there you go. It's right there in Cyrillic. Very faint but --

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There may be something, but to be honest, I don't see --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So you didn't see that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's do it, because I have examined this document before myself, and I think it will be easier if he holds it in -- if he holds the document in his hands.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, yes, there is. I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right? It doesn't show clearly if you put it on the ELMO, but if you look at it with your naked eye --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- you can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And you didn't notice that there was a water-mark on that document either, did you, I take it?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So you never held this document up to the light when you were analysing it?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, actually, I did, but I was looking to the -- the signature.

utterances.text: Could the witness please speak closer to the microphone?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Usher, can you hear me from here? We -- either the witness needs to come forward nearer to the microphones or the other way, we move the microphones nearer to him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'll come closer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And, again, please allow a little short pause between question and answer.

utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You were working in quite a hurry, were you not?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's why I concentrated because the first question was signatures and on the -- on the hearing on the 2nd of February, I got impression that the signatures are the main -- the main part of this examination. I did very much -- very much concentrate on the signatures, and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. And did you actually even leave time for retesting? A few days to cool off and then go back to your conclusion?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. To the signatures, yes, I did. I did -- I left the stuff aside completely and then come back to it. I mean, I don't have it with me, but I can give you a complete way I worked. I have that back home. Day by day, even hour by hour, what I -- how I did that, because that's how the notes are taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. No, believe me, the way -- we believe you 100 per cent so that's not an issue. I'd like to turn to P14 now, which is image 12, and in fact it's on pages 23, 24 and 25.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Of course we looked a lot at this document yesterday. You said inconclusive in relation to this document?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And at the same time you said that it matches only in some features of reference signatures. That's page 12 of your report. But in fact there are quite a few differences, aren't there, from the reference signatures?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the main difference apart from the fact that this is -- this particular signature is executed with seven strokes, which is quite significant, the main thing is, I believe, in this -- in this part when they actually -- I is completely missing, actually. There is only this part here seen which is basically a full stop between lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: There is also variations in the angles of slant, aren't there, and it's -- which are outside those of the reference signatures?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: A little bit, not very significantly. It's quite near but not a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Let's go to the more significant features. People usually do their signature with the same number of strokes?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And so extra strokes may therefore be indicative of someone trying to simulate or forge the signature and not doing it well; correct?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And then you even pick up in your report on what you call a "exceptionally unusual feature," and that's set out on page 12 of your report. In fact, that may be the one you just referred to.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is exceptionally unusual.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Is the pause of the writing implement at the "ch."

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But then you offer two explanations. One is the malfunctioning ball-point pen, or: "It is also possible that a template was used to produce the signature." Now, I want to be clear --

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I go just to the originals?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may. So it will come easier. 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's the very -- it's the penultimate sentence. "It is also possible that a template was used."

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Just to check what I wrote in Slovenian.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. And what you've marked there is actually an imitation or a forgery, isn't it, in other words. A person doesn't use a template to do their own signature?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I said, it -- this could be so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Isn't that explanation, template, more likely, given that you have these extra strokes?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this was a very difficult part of this examination. Precisely this signature. I was trying to be cautious not to be wrong, but I think there is a -- it is possible that certain -- certain limitation of the writing situation can result in that. Although to be honest -- to -- to think about it, that's why -- that's why I didn't say it is a falsified signature, but that is a quite strong possibility anyway. I couldn't establish it for sure because you have only this one but very strong full stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually -- may I finish, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually with the signatures written by template, usually you would see more of those. The simplification of this signature is quite high, comparing to all the others, either questioned or reference signatures. Would you agree with that, I think, it's quite simplified. Because of the simplification, one can also think that it's possible something was going wrong while writing this -- this signature. That's why I decided to go to inconclusive. But I fully agree with you, this signature can be forged. It can.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So why did you not conclude that the questioned and reference signatures were probably not written by the same person?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just explained that to you, didn't I?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, let's take it step by step, then. You conclude, and this is what you say: "Because no conclusion can be made with certainty, the result of the examination is inconclusive." I put it to you that's a very strange thing to say, because in your analysis result scale you have no problem with expressing probabilistic conclusions; you're okay with saying probably written, probably not written. There are not certain conclusions there and yet you make them. So it's -- that's not the reason, I suggest, that you've gone for inconclusive. It's for some quite other reason.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: And which reason that may be, if I may ask you?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That you were avoiding at all costs ever saying that the signature was possibly or probably not that of the author of the reference samples.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I disagree with that with you. But to be completely honest, I did a lot of thinking about this signature. This signature is quite of a problem, and it's really difficult to come to any conclusion. So I -- that's the reason why I go to the inconclusive. But anyway, it's very strange -- a strange one.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Let's also look at page 24 and 25 of your report where you draw -- you drew attention to some of these anomalies. And since you mentioned yesterday -- we don't need to go over the ones which you've already identified. But are there not, along with extra strokes, classic indications of imitation, namely double lines, double strokes on the O, first of all? And you can -- if you need, you can take a magnifying glass and look closely at the O?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I won't do that, it's quite unprofessional. But I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You disagree that actually there are double lines on the O that's been drawn over more than once --

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where can you find them? Can you indicate where you see them?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, on the O.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the O. Which part of the O?.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The outside.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apologies, but the O is all outside. It's a loop. Which part of the loop, if you can --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'll try and indicate to you. Can you see --

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe you're referring to this part, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, and slightly further down.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Over here.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. That's -- that's when I was -- analysed that under the microscope, it's actually the line that usually goes inside of the loop. This lines here.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And did you also notice -- well, yes, you have an arrow pointing to it, and I'm afraid we can't see the number on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which one --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That extra beginner stroke on the R.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this extra beginner stroke, what --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Number 4.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know which one. But you're pointing to this. The extra beginner stroke as I -- I fully described, and I've shown it also on the image 12B, I think. That is the one. I showed you the upper portion of that, because the -- the fact that this R starts down with this is not the problem. The problem is that it's -- it's not connected, this stroke is not connected to the R. It's an extra stroke, actually. That's my problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, my suggestion to you, and I think we've probably looked at this document enough is that the differences in fact dominate rather than the similarities between this signature and those of the reference signatures. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say they dominate, but they are quite significant. You were talking beforehand on I think P4 about the fact that there are the same number of similarities and dissimilarities and that it should go to the inconclusive. In this case, the similarities and the dissimilarities would be on [indiscernible]. But what worries me in this particular signature is the fact that it has this blunt full stop, which is the main problem from my point of view, and this extra stroke.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. I'm not going to ask to you do analysis in the courtroom because you made clear you wouldn't do that. But did you notice that the writing at the top doesn't align the right-hand -- if you see [B/C/S spoken] doesn't align with [B/C/S spoken] West Srebrenica on the left-hand side? Did you notice that? Did you look for that?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is document number P?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's P37.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: P14. Just let me. I see no -- I don't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I can lend you a ruler, if you would like, and you can see whether they actually align.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't really know what your implying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's stick to the signature business, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. I could --

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can believe you, but you have to realise this is a very old -- I know the type of the typewriter, and I know the problems of these typewriters. This is the typewriter produced by the Olympia, either Olympia [indiscernible]. I believe the former ones we had a lot of them in former Yugoslavia, and we had a lot of problems but they were old so this could -- I've typed misalignment quite often. But if you say, I would -- if you say that there is a misalignment, I won't disagree with you because I can't say it's not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, let's move to P37.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I assume the break is at 10.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, P37, if you give me one moment.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That one, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Pages 12, 13 of your report. And again this document you say that it matches the reference signatures only in some features. And, again, there are differences, big differences, are there not? Firstly, as you've noted, the signature is larger than the reference one?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but the proportions are not different.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to suggest to you that the features we saw in the reference samples are all different in this signature, and I can take it quickly. First do you agree the horizontal line is not tapering but solid and in fact it even has an additional squiggle at the end?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. There is a stroke connecting the R to the O, there is a line connecting the R to the O, there is no gap between the O and the R?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is no gap there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The -- what I was referring to as the kink in the I is not present?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because it's so simplified. It's -- this part of the signature is very badly seen, and I've shown it on the other image.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And again, the finishing stroke on the O is in fact even outside the O, whereas on the reference samples it's always a deep line going inside?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But it's the -- do you agree that it's the --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry, you're agreeing that it's outside?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I'm asking you if you agree that it is deeper.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
