utterances.text: I'm afraid you can't ask me questions.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Jones is correct. Please try to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm sorry. I didn't want to be -- I just wanted to point out whether it is nevertheless quite deep down, if ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you agree, it's just a matter of expression.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine. Point taken.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And then the fifth feature you've drawn attention to in your diagram 13A, which is on page 25.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That shows a pause, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, with all these differences, if you were being fair, if you were being objective, would you not say that this is probably not the same author as the author of the reference signatures rather than again going for inconclusive?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the deciding, the question which is not only related to this signature, deciding that somebody is certainly not rules out the fact that person can either -- but I will go back to this particular signature later. This is just theory. Sorry. The fact is that a person can or has to -- to amend something to the signature due to the different things, different circumstances, am I too far from this? And then the other thing is somebody can try to conceal his -- his -- his signature by exactly trying to do something like that. Although not to say that I'm implying that here. I don't think that happened here. I don't think. It is possible that the writing implement did have problems. Otherwise there is a blunt stop, like there. But I cannot rule out the possibility that this happened because of the different circumstances. I don't know the circumstances. In this P37 and P14, I think the P14 was discussed just a second ago, those two signatures are very problematic, and that's why again with both of them I went into the inconclusive because I cannot conclude either, either propositions.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So this one, this is possibly not by the same author as the reference signatures?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, as I said with P14, that is a certain possibility, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm coming to the next document, P73. Perhaps that's a good time for the break. I apologise I'm taking slightly longer than predicted, but in fact I think I'll be finished in 15 to 20 minutes after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Mr. Jones. I thank you, Dr. Kerzan. Please take the opportunity of having a rest. We will have a 25-minute break, if you don't mind, and then we will have the final questions and then we have another break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. We just have six more documents to go through.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Firstly, we are going to look at P73.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But I've got a couple of questions about P73, P74, P75 generally, because they have certain similar features.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And it's just two basic points for the record. Firstly, these three documents all purportedly bear the signature of Hamdija Fejzic. And it's an obvious point, but just to confirm, you haven't analysed that signature and you can't tell us anything about that its authenticity or otherwise?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I did not -- I was instructed on February 2nd not to do that, and I certainly didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. And the second preliminary point, and again it's an obvious one, but I take it you didn't carbon date any of these documents, and so as to the purported dates when they were signed, you can't tell us anything about whether they were, if it was signed by the purported author, whether it was in 1992 or 1993 or 1994 or 1995 and simply back-dated. That's not something you can help us with?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, of course not. And on the other hand, you cannot do that by carbon dating, because it's a 60 years time-frame which is in question then if we -- with carbon dating you can't do that. It's a archeological thing, not a forensic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. So even where you --

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You can't reach a conclusion, you have no idea when it was signed?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, P73, and I'm going to make a conscious effort to go very slowly because I know it was very difficult for the stenographer this morning. P73 is page 13 of your report and it's image 14.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I put it --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. On page 26. And again I'm going to put it to you that the five or six features which I pointed out on the reference samples are all different here. First, can you confirm that the horizontal line is not tapered but it's blunt; in fact, it even ends in a blob?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that completely. There is a blob at the end, but you can see in the middle right where the arrow number 7 points to it that it gets lighter. So at the end of it is a blunt -- is a more of a stop, but it again -- it is getting lighter so the dynamics is present here, dynamics what you're talking about, if I made myself clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I'm not, just --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The tapering earlier on but it doesn't, the end isn't tapered, the end of the line is not tapered?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The end, it was tapered but then it stopped. So, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And you could probably see more clearly with your instruments, but can you confirm that the R is not connected to the O -- oh, sorry. The R, on the contrary, is connected, that there is actually a line connecting the two?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would say that I agree with that. It touches. It's not connected. Again, it's a difference saying connected or it touches.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Okay. It touches?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's quite a big difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Again, looking at the -- what I was referring to as a kink in the I, that's not -- that doesn't appear in the loop, does it? The loop is clear and continuous and there is no kink?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's just before likeness on at least one of the reference signatures.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And again, I put it to you that the O is actually more circular than ellipsoid?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. With this one I disagree.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And the closing stroke is not deep and penetrating. It's --

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's here. It's finished somewhere here, so it's quite deep.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Does it in fact finish there, or does it in fact finish earlier on?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I think somewhere here. But have to look at it through the microscope to be confirmed. But I think it finishes right -- around this line.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So it's not particularly deep.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Relatively, I would say. Doesn't go very, very down.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And, of course, there is the dot which you've marked with arrow 11?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, obviously.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, on this document, you've told us yesterday that you didn't notice or didn't look for the mark -- sorry, where Skelani has been placed on this document, and I don't propose to dwell on it. Do you have the photocopy of the whole document?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have. Let me just wait for --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I simply want to put this to you: That firstly you don't know what was written beforehand, do you, behind Skelani?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And secondly, I suggest to you that if you don't know what was written beforehand you can't say whether there was manipulation or not. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I can't say whether it is not -- it is or not a manipulation.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. Because on page 13 of your report you said: "There is no visible evidence of falsification or manipulation on the document." Now, is that correct, or would it be better to say that it's not something which you in fact addressed in your report?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say I did not address that in my report thoroughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, your criticism here is in place.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's not a criticism. It's just a clarification for the report. Thank you. We can move on to P74, and that's image 15. And if it seems I'm labouring the points about these differences, I'm coming to the point in a moment with this document. But would you agree again the horizontal line, not tapered but blunt?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It ends bluntly. But, again, there are visible, visible tapering before it ends, so there is uncertain end.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Okay. I'm just talking about the end.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: There is a tail or a stroke which means that the R and the O touch, the R and the O are touching?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's -- I don't think it touches but it's extremely near. It is just -- it's badly -- it's hard to see but it's started here and they are so near but it's extremely small gap. This gap is not very significant in this case, but there is a small, smallish gap.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So there is actually a left-hand stroke on the R going from the O before it then goes -- before it's drawn. There is a stroke going away from the O and then it goes down into the rest of the document?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this initial stroke in R?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is initial stroke in R exists. Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Again, the kink in the "ch" is not present. You would say it's to the left?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a bit to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's not in the loop; that's my point.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not in the loop, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And, again, the closing stroke in the O is not particularly deep, not like on the reference samples?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not all the reference samples is so deep, but it's relative deep. It penetrates for approximately one-third or even -- approximately one-third of the loop, so it is -- this is, from my point of view, deep.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But it's not almost like a third vertical?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in this case, not. But it touches this vertical.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't overlap it but it touches for approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now I'm sure you appreciate with these points I'm making, there are two points really. Firstly is whether the reference samples and the questioned samples have these features in common. But there is another point which is what I want to take up with you now, which is that if the questioned samples all have the same characteristics, in other words, if there are similarities between the reference samples which don't exist vis-a-vis the reference samples, that can be indicative of a forger making the same mistakes in his simulation. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I re-read your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's a long question. Tell you what, it's easier if I simply read from Ellen who expresses it much better. And that's page 54 of Ellen.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I know what you're going to quote.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's the section "identification of the writer of simulations." It says: "Free-hand simulations of a signature made by one person will generally be found to be consistent with each other, differing both from the copied signature and simulations of the same genuine signature made by other people. This is not only because the copier may leave evidence of his own writing but also because people appear to be consistent in the way they copy writing and the errors they make." Do you agree with that proposition, first of all?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but may I just make a note now, because I would have to comment on this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Then before you answer, I just want to carry on with Ellen. On page 36 we are directed to figure 5 where we see simulations, as it happens, and the figure there states: "On the right-hand side of the picture a genuine signature is shown. On the left are two attempts at a free-hand simulation made by three different people." It says: "Note, one, the inaccuracies; two, the poor line quality; and three," three is what I'm interested in, "the similarities of the deviations and the genuine letter D within each pair." And so that's the point, isn't it, when someone imitates a signature, they tend to make the same mistakes when they do so. And feel free to comment at length, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I will not comment very much at length. I anticipated that question. It's -- therefore, it's a very good point, but if that was to be consistent, you wouldn't expect that on P158 the dot would be missing. It is highly unusual that a forger would miss such a thing that he used on another samples. And the same goes with the missing initial stroke in R on P75. So I don't think that your point really is -- I disagree with your point. I'm just pointing on the fact that they are showing quite the opposite.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I understand that. But aren't you now attributing a significance to the full stop which earlier you deemed insignificant?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just mentioned that part. I did not put any -- it can be significant. I don't think how significant -- I don't want to comment on that, but I'm just pointing to that fact, because you're also pointing to the things that can or cannot be significant. It is not the matter of significance at this point. I'm just pointing to the particular features.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Do you accept the possibility that what we have here is a free-hand simulator trying to copy the signature of Naser Oric but making the same habitual and even unconscious possibly mistakes each time? And I'm referring to these six or seven differences which I keep pointing out.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I said, I disagree with your six or seven differences. And I explained that there is no -- there are differences in execution of those -- those signatures we are talking about, signatures I think from P73 to P158, those four, I think they are, am I correct here?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Well, let's look at P75. We can move on to that now, because I suggest that with maybe one exception that the same differences are there. Again, the horizontal is not tapering?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is. Excuse me, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. We can disagree there. That the -- in this case, certainly I concede the R is not touching the O. We can see that?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a gap, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The third line on the O is not like a third vertical?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not deep here. But I would like really to point to the fact that the initial stroke of R is missing - this is quite important here - in this particular signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And, again, the kink in the I is not within the loop. You would say it's to the left, and you're indicating that on figure 37, I think?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I just, once again, comment on that kink? That fact that those kinks are out would be very important in my report if there wasn't at least one reference signature with such a feature. If I didn't find any reference signatures with that feature, I would fully agree that kink, as you call it, is important feature. But as there is one, I -- I went not to decide that this is so important to draw conclusion from that. If I made myself clear. I --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. So one is like that in the reference samples but seven are not?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But this fact that one is shows the variability of signature. So if we have very probably, if we have more signatures, there would be more of them, not all but more. Okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Do you also agree P75 is quite a bit smaller, if you compare it, for example, with P14, it's -- P14 is huge by comparison?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I wrote that P14 is very big so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: This is quite a bit smaller, isn't it, and there is no reason why is it should be small. There is no particularly confined space in which it is to be written?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's relatively small. Most of them are relatively small, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Okay. And then -- well, you dealt with Srebrenica, the manipulation there -- well, not manipulation; I apologise. I suggest it's a manipulation or might be but it's not something which you've analysed?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't comment really on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, we can move on, I believe, to P158.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And we have dealt with the absence of a full stop, so I won't dwell on that. But, once again, I will go through these differences which I submit are there. Horizontal is ending bluntly not in tapering end?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In this case I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The -- what I've been calling the kink in the I is to the left of the loop; it's not inside it. Again, I accept your explanation, but do you agree?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree. But, again, I refer to my explanation of the one before.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The R touches the O. There is that initial stoke stroke on the R?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The finishing stroke on the O isn't like a third vertical?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, can I comment on that? It's not like a third vertical. It's a little bit outside but it's relatively deep. The importance here is that it goes deep inside. And that's what I wanted to point out here. It's relatively deep. It goes almost half of the letter O now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And I won't use the term "garlands," but in terms of the waves, the waviness, do you say that matches the reference samples?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the way the hand moved, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So for you the similarities predominate despite these differences which I pointed out between this and the reference samples?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If we look at this document, even the below the signature line it says "Nasre Oric," which I believe is practically a dirty word in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. Well, let me put it this way: If my name is John, my first name, if I were to sign something which is written J-h-o-n, I'm sure I would correct it, I'm sure you would correct it if your first name were miswritten. Does that reflect -- do you reflect on that in your analysis, or is that not something you take into account?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't -- I don't find that very important. And if you ask me personally, my name was so often misspelled that I don't take -- care about that anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's perhaps a feature of the name rather than anything else.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I didn't pay any attention to that. I didn't find that important.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If I suggest to you that P158, P73, 74, 75, P4, they all have consistent similarities between each other, and those are all consistently different from the reference samples. Do you have any comment on that?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they are quite similar but as I have already noted, there are also differences which would be probably inconsistent with the proposition that it was a free-hand forgery. I find -- I do not find the -- consistently different features. There are some features which can be interpreted as different, but they are within the -- within the variations of the -- of the reference samples, in my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. I think we can look briefly at P210.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's on pages 16 to 17 of your report. And, again, this is inconclusive. And I think your suggestion is again that's because it's a copy or because the stamp partly covers the signature; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Isn't the reality that there are actually a lot of differences between this signature and the reference samples?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the photocopy covers a lot of significant -- a lot of -- or some of the -- of the features of this signature, I cannot comment that. It can be but I can't see them. I can't really say there are or there are not. It is the material which is completely unsuitable for examination. I mean, or it would be more guessing like than proper examination. That's why I did not want to go deep into the -- into that. The same with I think P3, too. P3, I think it's also the photocopy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Very well. We can move on to P269, finally.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And I submit to you that this is, if you forgive the expression, there is a joke to say that this could possibly or to consider this could possibly be the same as the reference signature by the author of the reference samples. It's a completely different signature, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And you've never seen this signature in any of the reference samples, have you?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This signature is executed completely differently, if I may just --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: And it is impossible to make any comparison. It is like if you write a word in cursive and in block capitals. That's the difference. It's incomparable. That is the -- perhaps I shouldn't write inconclusive. I should write incomparable. It's not possible to conduct any examination. But I find this signature in the fact that it's written with the name and surname odd, within the realm of all the signatures we are dealing with here today.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. Didn't you explain yesterday when you were explaining when your conclusions strongly support the assumption that the questioned and reference signatures are not written by the same individual, you said that might happen, for example, where someone comes along and just knows the name and does a signature, purported signature of that name, and it doesn't correspond at all to the signature of that individual. Shouldn't you have said here this is not written by the same person?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because I don't see any features because of the facts. If that was not -- if that was the originals, I perhaps could have reached that conclusion. I fully agree with you on that one. But it is the facts I see no features. It's completely different. And as I said, it's incomparable. So if it's incomparable, I cannot be conclusive on anything, if I made myself understandable here.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. You did also suggest yesterday as one possibility that this document, since it was sent to Sarajevo, that that might somehow explain this difference. And you'll recall yesterday I asked you about it being important for purposes of banks, et cetera, to actually maintain the same signature in order for that to be recognised. Now, surely your explanation cuts both ways: That if something is sent to Sarajevo, that's all the more reason why you should have a recognisable signature?

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, now, what you're referring to, my answers yesterday, this was as was clear yesterday also, it was my speculation. It was not something I can prove or disprove in any way. But in certain situations, like, for example, on wills, you see people that are having a short -- short -- short signatures that will -- that they will use a longer version, or they will use a name and surname. But, of course, this is speculation. This particular signature is, as I explained already, out of the order of all the others. Because it is a fax it is against the doctrine of the forensic handwriting examination to go into the identification process. But it is out of any of the -- of the other signatures we are dealing with, either questioned or reference. So ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's clear. Two final matters. Yesterday I read from a passage in Ellen on subjectivity and how the personality of the examiner has an influence. I put it to you that your approach, your subjectivity, which everyone has, but it's such that you've tended to minimise the differences between the reference and the questioned signatures and to exaggerate and dwell upon the similarities. That's my suggestion to you firstly.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I disagree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. And secondly I put it to you that P4, P73, P74, P75 and P158, among others, but those are the ones where you've given your opinion that they are signed by Naser Oric, that those were not signed by him, not then or ever, and that your opinion is mistaken and that I ask you whether you accept the possibility that your opinion is mistaken, that you're wrong when you say that those are the same signatures.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I answer this question at length?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DORIJAN KERZAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I always accept possibility that I'm wrong. It would be -- I think it's impossible to state somebody is right, complete 100 per cent right. I think my opinion was prepared with caution and with knowledge and the experience I have and the method which is appropriate for that. But I cannot rule out the possibility of being wrong. Everybody makes mistakes, so -- but this is a matter of doctrine in my opinion. I cannot rule out that possibility whatsoever. I wouldn't even dare to say there is 100 per cent, if I saw the accused, because I don't know to -- there is no certainty in any way in this way. That's what I wanted to stress here.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I thank you very much. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would like to thank you for your questions too. It was the thoroughest examination I have ever been to. Thank you very much. It was very interesting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Dr. Kerzan, your testimony ends here because we don't have any questions for you either. I wish to thank you on behalf of the Trial Chamber for having, first of all, accepted to do this work for us and for having carried it out in a timely fashion, and last but not least for having also come over and testified. Before you leave this courtroom, apart from thanking you, I also wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And I would also like to thank the Honourable Court that they -- that you appointed me. It was a real honour for me to the opportunity to work for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How long a pause do you require, Mr. Wubben?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Around 30 minutes would be fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Because I have this problem. I had a burst water-pipe in my apartment first thing this morning, at 6.00 this morning, and I need to attend to it. So and I have a plumber plus security accompanying me to my apartment to have this job done at 1.00. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we try to support in that respect that we will be within 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. 15 minutes would bring us -- then we should finish this matter. Or else we adjourn it until tomorrow. I mean, that's the other possibility. Until tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I would rather prefer not. I can't speak for the Defence but I rather prefer to finalise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I was also wondering, Your Honour, whether some of these issues could be regulated even through e-mails and through the legal officer and -- outside the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: They possibly could. But anyway, let's have the 15-minute break and see what we can -- but I will try to leave here not later than quarter to 1.00. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So before we embark on the -- this short exercise, I as Presiding Judge, I have a statement to make for the record only. Otherwise, we wouldn't need to go into any details. But the Trial Chamber will not be calling any witnesses of its own. This decision was taken by majority. The majority of us decided so, with Judge Eser dissenting. So that goes on for the record. Now, there is some cleaning -- housekeeping exercises that we need to do. Let me go -- yes, I see Mr. Wubben standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, Thank you. It's for the record that my team is now extended with Ms. Patricia Sellers and Mr. Jose Doria. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Wubben. Let's start from here. The reason why we sort of suggested this special exercise is that you know, of course, that as we go along we are always digging up into our records to make sure that everything is in order by way of exhibits, that CDs are working, function properly, DVDs the same, and so on and so forth. And as we went along, of course, and as we go along, we start discovering some shortcomings. I'll start with the first one. Way back on the 21st of February, or, rather, we have been expecting the 94 bis statement of Dr. Zoran Stankovic, which has never arrived. Yes, Ms. Sellers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We had granted this, as you will recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In discussing this with the team members we realised that, and we will be able to present this to the Trial Chamber, and I will have to ask for a P number for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. So that will be dealt with at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I believe we do have the copies here and we could hand them up at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, if you can do that, let's do it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thanks. And what number shall we give this, please, Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be P623, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this statement will become P623, all right?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. You will recall, because this was also a matter of one of the very last motions that we dealt with, that we were promised by you a revised English translation of P84 and P598. What's the position?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the position on that is that, I believe, several weeks ago we did try to ask at that time period for P598 to substitute the copy we found that had included two pages that were missing in the original. And if I correctly recall the position, we thought that we would have to give it P598.1 or another number. At that point in time, I believe the Defence objected to it, wanted to look at the original. The Defence has had a time granted to them where they did review the original of the document and that is why the Prosecution would now say that we would like to move the complete document that we would refer to as P591 into evidence. And I've been informed by Defence counsel that they had some comments on the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, first of all, we do not accept that document P598, or, rather, the pages that the Prosecution wants to tender today, that they form part of P598 at all. You'll remember me talking about it the other day, and we have it on the record, and, for the sake of the time, I don't want to dwell on it any more. Because I had my suspicions about the fact that these pages did not in fact form part of the exhibit, I asked the other time to be shown the original. The Prosecution handed me a photocopy of a similar exhibit, I would say, which in any case was not at all a photocopy of P598. It differed greatly from what is now being offered for admission. P598 was an exhibit with precisely numerated pages, whereas the P598 that was shown to our witness had only page numeration from 5 onwards. In dealing with our witness, D005, this document started from page 1. Again, I claim that these are two different documents and these pages should not be mixed up in this way. This prompted me to ask for an inspection of all the Prosecution documents that became exhibits marked with P. I apologise, I was trying to save time and went too speedily. I do not wish to dwell on it today. I inspected the documents, and as a result I have very important data to present to the Trial Chamber, and I hope that we will submit it to this Trial Chamber within seven days, as part of our filing, and it is quite interesting to see that on many occasions the Prosecution does not have -- or, rather, I will not go into that today. What I wish to say, furthermore, is that I saw something that had to do with P598. Evidence unit, in the presence of two OTP members, Mr. Berikoff and a forensic technician, showed me what they thought was the original of P598, and that was not the same copy that was shown to me as the original here in the courtroom. In fact, it was a photocopy of this very document that was shown to our witness as P598. This is what they have listed as the original. We oppose any attempt to add subsequent pages to this exhibit because, simply, this is not one and the same exhibit. We have had this exhibit for years, and I know what I'm saying because we have double-checked that. We will refer to that in our filing. This was no way of proceeding to do it right now. This should have been dealt with at the time when we had the witness here. They want to prove with this document that Kemo Mehmedovic was member of the Potocari unit, which cannot be found at all in P598, and none of the witnesses were shown that. This is not a proper way of proceeding, to add to the existing exhibits without putting these pages to the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But the exercise -- I don't want to hear any more on this. The exercise that we are going through today is not to receive submissions on the admissibility or otherwise of these documents. I just stated in the beginning that we have on record that at one time, without, of course, prejudice to the submissions that have been made by the Defence on P598 and these extra two pages with the variations of reference number and with or without, et cetera, that you had promised to come forward with a revised English translation of same, and we are still expecting that. So this is precisely what we are addressing now. We would like to know when we would be in a position to have -- or when you would be in a position to provide us with these translation, of course keeping completely unprejudiced the position of the Defence in relation to any of these documents or parts thereof.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we do have those revised translations today. We can hand them up to the Chamber, and we will reserve any arguments, responses to Madam Vidovic, whether it be in writing or whether the parties should contact each other to discuss it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Then in relation to P127 and 279. Now, on the face of it, these two exhibits really are -- consist of the same document. However, they do have different ERN numbers and different dates. We need a clarification from you, from the Prosecution, on this, and how you expect these two documents to be treated.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution would ask that you accept P279, with the ERN number 00520764 to 00520765, as the Prosecution's exhibit. We received, in essence, the same document twice, and that is why it came to have two different numbers. But would you please now refer to that evidence as P279.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Do you have a position on this, in case -- before I close on this part, Ms. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I really have to review the translation, and I cannot give my response to that at this time. We've already had similar experience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I think that's maybe a different point. We need to just check that, I think, on P127.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. Let me make our position clear. The fact that we have now received this declaration from the Prosecution does not mean that automatically we therefore strike off from the record P127. That will remain there. We take it, however, that when there may be reference to this particular document, you will be referring to it as P279 from your part. That's how I take it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Now, this document that has been circulated now, starting with "Pale" at the top, this is P84 or what is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is what we will be referring to as substitution for P598.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, that we oppose vigorously. We say that's not P598 at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this is -- I've marked mine as P598 with a question mark and "opposed" in brackets or "objected." All right. P328 and 329. These are the -- you know what they are. You will recall that quite recently, basically on the 13th of December, parts of these exhibits were replaced by new sets, or the Prosecution sought to replace parts of these exhibits with new sets, and on the 1st of February, again we faced the same situation. The Prosecution sought to produce new sets and have them admitted instead of the previous ones. I don't need to go back to the discussion. I recall the discussion, the debate, that we had here. But we decided then, for various reasons, that the two sets would co-exist with the original ones, for various reasons. You can refer to the transcripts of the two sittings, 13 December and 1st of February. I am being told that parts submitted in December are the same as the ones submitted in February. So we would like to know from your part, Ms. Sellers or whoever, what is your position on this and what you are actually tendering and seeking to replace.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would draw the Trial Chamber's attention to what was tendered in February as being a complete set, and I would therefore ask that the Trial Chamber and also Defence counsel disregard what was tendered in January, which tried to make some of the rectifications of what had been tendered in December, and if we would now just concentrate on February as having been the complete set.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Of course, asking the Defence to disregard, it's up to them to do that or not to do that. In the meantime, we need to make it clear that since we ultimately have to reach our decisions, the various sets will co-exist, will continue to co-exist. In other words, we will decide what the position is in due course after having received any submissions that the Defence might have on this matter, also because there may ultimately be the need to make comparative analysis between one and the other, if that comes into question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, might I interrupt you for one second? I believe when we handed up the English translation of what we are referring to to facilitate our task here as P598, do we need to ask for a number for that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. I'm coming to that. In fact now, particularly since you seem to lay emphasis on the February filings, or exhibits, they have to be renumbered, or, rather, they have to be numbered, given a new number. You will recall that previously, when we had the first set sought to be replaced, we had put -- given them P328.1 and 329.1. Now, the February ones will become P328.2 and P329.2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You want a new number for them? All right. Which would be what? What number do you require from us?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be P624, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So these will become P624 and -- both of them? Both of them. So the whole set, the whole collection of CDs supposedly sought to be replacement of P328 and 329, right, will become P624.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would prefer it that way, but I would require to know which set becomes 624 and which set becomes 625. No, leave it. Ms. Vidovic, would you be able -- and Ms. Sellers, would you be able to live with this one new number for the whole CD set that was filed in February?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would. It would be easier, I think, with the two numbers and one would know when they are in old P329 that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But you would have to indicate which ones would be 624 and which ones would be 625.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I think two numbers would be better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, I agree too.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll check and see if we could indicate that. That just might be a very --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's put it like this: Then one set which seeks to replace P328 will be P624; and the other set which seeks to replace P329, and 329.1 obviously, will be P625. And that will become so when you have indicated which ones, of course, with all due notice to -- information to --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. We'll circulate that both to Defence and to the Registry and Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we go back to P598? We are extremely unhappy about what's being done here. It's one thing to offer up what purports to be a new English translation, but we see there is a Bosnian with it, and this, again, is a different exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Don't worry, Mr. Jones. Let them file what they want for the time being, and then, if there are submissions, we will come to the submissions later.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Could we not call it P598, then? Because this is a different document, and it's too late for the Prosecution to tender new exhibits, and they are trying to tender a new exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If it's a new exhibit, we won't allow it, unless there is a special request for that. That's the procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So may I just say on the record that if you compare the English to P598, you'll see it's not the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You just make a submission, and if the submission ultimately leads us to consider that as a new document, Prosecution seeking to admit a new document when their case has actually ended, then you know what the procedure is. I'm not teaching anyone here.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. I was just worried that by being given that number, it was becoming an exhibit surreptitiously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I must say I do not understand this point because we have requested --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The translation of the existing P98 [sic], but if it's a different P98, then we are talking of a different document. This is what is being -- P456.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, might I clarify this? Excuse me for interrupting. The translation -- okay -- is a translation of the document that would be the new P598. I don't want in any way to disagree at this point with what Defence counsel is saying and probably Judge Eser also. There is the new P598 which has no number because it's been in discussion now for several weeks, and this was the English translation of what would be the new P598.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But a translation is a translation. It's not the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Absolutely right, Your Honour. Therefore we now do not have a document that goes with the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What Mr. Jones is saying is that this is not a translation of the existing P98 that you are offering but something in addition to that, which would make it a different document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm agreeing to the extent that this is a translation of what we are calling the complete 598 that we sought to substitute. I don't want to belabour any submissions but just to make sure we are clear administratively of what this is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But deal with it amongst yourselves, and then, if necessary, we will give you a hearing on this. P456. I'm told that you need to provide us with pages 8 and 9 of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have that now, and we would be willing to hand that up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So pages 8 and 9 of P456. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we are also being given, for the record, the translation of P84. All right. Let's move. P561. Now, the problem, this I have mentioned on several occasions before, and ultimately we had agreed that we will know at some point in time what the situation would be. P561 corresponds to P458, according to our record. You need to clarify whether the whole logbook is tendered as P458, or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that we should now refer to it as P561.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you made that statement before.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But if you have submissions on that, Madam Vidovic, please come forward later on, okay? So P570. Again, I had mentioned this -- yes, Ms. Vidovic? Please, if you have submissions on it, I'd like to reserve them for later so that we finish this exercise today. All right? P570. You had promised us a long time ago the B/C/S version of this document. Supposedly it was ready and readily available at the time but we never got it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's readily available today, and we'll hand it up now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So in the meantime while this is being distributed, let's proceed. P586 and P589.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We can also hand up the English translation for P586 and 589.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. So this has been attended to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So all of them except the one which is already marked form part of P589.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, P600, 605 and 607. Of course, we are fully aware that there were objections from the Defence in regards to what was sought. Let me go through it. When these exhibits were first tendered on 29/11 of last year they were not complete. The OTP tendered on the 13th December new sets of these exhibits. Mr. Jones, on the record, objected to the new sets being tendered and we had ruled as follows: We expect to hear back from you, Mr. Jones, if you have an objection, when I say, Mr. Jones, if you have an objection about having these three documents replacing the previous ones, for the time being, of course, the previous ones will remain in the record and the matter will become final when we meet again in January. The Defence needs to clarify now whether they object or not to these new sets of exhibits replacing the previous ones or not so that we can take a decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We maintain our objections and for the reasons stated on the day. I believe I gave some of our reasons, and we maintain our objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So the position is for the time being they will co-exist. All right?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: P377. Prosecutors, on the 22nd of October, that's very early when we had just started the case, the Prosecutor submitted a map which was given Exhibit number P377. The Defence objected to the markings contained in the document. Upon instruction, our instructions, the Prosecution withdrew the map and declared that it would be providing a new copy without comments. The new copy has never reached us, or at least that's the impression that we have. And the map from the Registry's binder is marked as never having been submitted. There is one, in other words, but it doesn't seem to have been submitted. So you need to provide us with the replacement of P377 without, of course, the markings which had formed the basis of the Defence objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, today we can hand that map out, having removed the -- as a matter of fact, the names of the attack sites, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that. Now, I turn on to you. There isn't much in your case and some things I know you will need to attend to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So just for clarity and precision: The new documents relating to P600, 605 and 607 which we have now decided will co-exist and not replace, okay, will be 600.1, 605.1 and 607.1, all right? Thank you. Thank you for this. It's P377. All right. Now, D38, Madam Vidovic or Mr. Jones, please feel free, would it be possible to have D38 in CD format?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. I believe for these matters we are working with the AV unit and we need to get copies from that unit as we are unable to change from DVD to CD.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Me too.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So we are working with the AV unit on that matter and as well as the next one which concerned D200, D702, 703, D866 and D870.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. I appreciate that, and I'm grateful to you, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might clarify, our impression was that the prior map had attack places and dates on it and that's what was removed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you object to the fact that there is that arrow --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- showing the -- all right. Okay. Thank you. So D271, 698 and 699. We are still waiting for the appropriate CDs, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That we are endeavouring to do as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Again, that's something which we will have to provide in the coming days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I appreciate that. And I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We are checking the matter in D690 as well as D597, so I can't actually provide you with information. We are working on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And I believe the issue under D960 is something for the Trial Chamber to clarify; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, the exhibit number came out wrong on the transcript but I wanted to inform you of this. From the transcript from the 5th of December. It appears D967 when it should have appeared as D960. All right? So for the record, we are making this statement. And you take notice of it accordingly. D1008.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. And that, too, we need to -- this is V0003971, I think, and we need to see which part we used and then to work out the technical part of that. For the last matter, I can say that we would maintain that these exhibits should be kept under seal, so I'm skipping down one, but they concern -- well, I needn't say what our position is, that they should remain under seal, and if you would wish me to address you on that, then I certainly can do. But that's our position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And with regard to D1012, I would like also to state that on the 23rd of January, the OTP objected to this exhibit. The objection came out wrong in the transcript. And needs to be clarified accordingly for the record. So we are making that statement. Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The -- what had been stated in the transcript was correct. I listened to the audio tape what was expressed -- what had been expressed by me came out using a wrong word. What was trying to say is that at that day and the previous day we expressed that we contest admittance of the report and focus our argumentation on the label of non-contentious documents used in the report by Professor Bilic, but there is an exception of the eight K documents, because we admit that these are known signatures. So these that's -- that's what is meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. We had exchanged some debate on whether it would be possible for you to agree on providing the Trial Chamber with a list of military acronyms; let me call them like that. Last I heard was that you had not ultimately come to an agreement. So do I take it that we will not be receiving this from you?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. We copied you on the letter we sent to the Defence, and the Defence finally in their response disagree. So we have to solve this matter whenever in the closing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. So what I mean to say is that there is no document containing agreed upon military acronyms before us; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I just wonder if Your Honour has a copy of our letter in response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I had the full correspondence on it. And obviously we did not intervene because this is ultimately something that you either agree upon or disagree upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can't force it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It was just so you knew our reasons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can't force it on anyone. The only option that we have is to appoint an expert ourselves but that would take ages. All right. The other thing is that you had given an indication again, and of course we cannot ask you more than what I'm going to say, that you would be coming forward probably with a kind of a document dealing with the contested documents. We just wanted to know whether this is still in the pipe-line.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Whether you still intend to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, we will be filing it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. I also wanted to confirm to you that this would not count for the purpose of page limitation for the final brief, in other words. All right? It will be completely separate. Other thing is this: No one has asked us from -- for an extension of the existing page limits for the final briefs. If you have an intention of putting such an amount, please come forward the sooner the better, all right?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Just to say, Your Honour, yesterday we discussed briefly with the Prosecution whether we would have a common position on requesting an extension, because we would be seeking that, and we will take that up with the Prosecution and get back to you as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm grateful if you come to some kind of agreement between you on this. It will be much better, much easier for us. So more problems?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. They will be placed permanently on seal, yes. The last documents on that list will be placed on seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In Sweden they train their staff well. I'm being asked to mention the documents one by one for the record. It's D221 to D224, both included. D226 to D228, both included. D231, D778, D786 to D790, both included. Yesterday I made a brief announcement saying that there will be a change, dramatic change, in the formation of the Prosecution team, and that we had received notice that Mr. Wubben will be leaving this Tribunal. Actually, it's only a few days ago that we learnt of Mr. Wubben's imminent departure, not only from this case but from the Tribunal, and admittedly I must say this came somewhat as an unpleasant surprise to us. After serving for four years in the OTP, the Office of the Prosecutor, in this Tribunal, Mr. Wubben will be returning to pastures already familiar to him, namely, the Dutch prosecutor services, the Openbaar Ministerie, in a more senior position than he held before. On the 22nd of this month, he wrote a courteous farewell letter in which he said: "It will be sad to say farewell to the OTP and to the challenges of the Prosecution as of the 17th of March," still more than three weeks for him to enjoy advocacy. "It is also sad to have to leave at the closing stage of this case but there is no doubt that the qualities of the team, including new lead counsel, will ensure the continuation of the Prosecution, at the required professional level. "I am pleased," said Mr. Wubben, "that I will be still in a position to complete the filing of the closing brief on the 17th of March. And then he continues: "In the coming weeks, I will thus be fully available as lead counsel. I look forward as well to meeting you in court. The contact with you all have been no doubt will be in the weeks to come a pleasure and a privilege." A pleasure and a privilege. Indeed, Mr. Wubben, this is also the feeling of this Bench in your regard. For us it was a pleasure and a privilege to work with you in this case in your capacities as lead counsel for the Prosecution. You've had the benefit of having at your disposal a very good team of lawyers and other assistants whom you have inspired and managed so well. You have worked very hard in this case, and it must not have been easy for you to adapt from the Dutch system to the ICTY system, which is a hybrid one with some peculiar procedures of its own. You have been honest, meticulous, and your loyalty towards the Trial Chamber has been conspicuous. Most importantly, you have succeeded in steering the Prosecution case in what at times were pretty troubled waters, and you did so with honesty, dignity and dexterity. When you leave this Tribunal on the 17th of March, almost all the work of the Prosecution in this case, including, as you said, the filing of the final brief, would have been concluded. We thank you for this and for having, throughout, made it possible for this Trial Chamber to adhere to its time schedule as much as possible. Mr. Wubben, it is always sad to say good-bye to someone like you in particular, after having lived this case together for a year and four months. But that has become inevitable now. So we bid you farewell and good-bye, Mr. Wubben, and we also wish you every success in your new venture in the Openbaar Ministerie. We have no doubt that just as this Tribunal benefited from your previous experience as a Dutch prosecutor, during your stay here, the Dutch prosecutor services, the Openbaar Ministerie, to which you are now returning, will benefit greatly from the experience you must have gained in these last four years in the Tribunal's Office of the Prosecutor. Consider this to be your legacy, Mr. Wubben. The OTP's loss is the Openbaar Ministerie's gain. And with this, we bid you farewell. You will be succeeded as lead counsel in this case by Trial Attorney Patricia Sellers, who was worked along your side in this case from its very beginning, and who we heartily welcome and congratulate. We are sure that she will continue to steer the case, the Prosecution case, professionally, with the same honesty, the same dignity and the same loyalty as you have shown, Mr. Wubben. We wish you good luck and every success. Yes, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may, I would like to add a sentence on behalf of the Defence team and on behalf of our client, Mr. Naser Oric. We would like to thank Mr. Wubben for the cooperation that he extended to us, and we wish him all the best in his life and in his future career.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Ms. Vidovic. And with that, I think we can adjourn. If -- as I said, if you require more pages for the final briefs, please let us know in good time, and if you have any queries in relation to the rest of the proceedings, as they are scheduled to progress, please also come forward, and we'll try to be as cooperative as we can. We will be, of course, working here, all of us, and at your disposal anxiously waiting for the final briefs, which from previous experience I can say are of extreme, extreme importance for the Judges, for the trial Judges. I thank you.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 12.40 p.m.
